en: The Scripture on the Five Kinds of Meritorious Retribution Obtained from Giving Food, as Spoken by the Buddha;
the translator’s name is lost, now appended to the Catalogue of the Eastern Jin.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. The Buddha...
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"You should know that food should be taken with moderation; one should receive it without waste.
Thus spoke the Buddha.

"When a person provides food and drink as an offering to others, there are five merits that enable them to attain the Way; if a wise person carefully examines their intent and makes it vast and expansive, they shall obtain these five blessings."
What are the five? First is the gift of life; second is the gift of beauty; third is the gift of strength; fourth is the gift of peace; and fifth is the gift of eloquence.
"What is meant by 'bestowing life'?

When a person does not obtain food, their complexion becomes withered and emaciated, such that they can no longer be shown to others; before seven days have passed, their life suddenly comes to an end. Therefore, the wise bestow food; to bestow food is to bestow life."

As for the gift of life, one will enjoy long life in every successive birth, being reborn in the heavenly realms where one's lifespan is extended and free from premature death or injury; naturally receiving immeasurable wealth as a karmic reward—this is called the gift of life.
"What is meant by 'bestowing color'?
When a person does not obtain food, their complexion becomes haggard and unsightly; therefore, the wise bestow food. To bestow food is to bestow color."

As for the gift of physical form: from lifetime to lifetime one will be handsome and upright, born in the heavens or the human world; with a countenance so radiant and brilliant that people see it and rejoice, bowing their heads in prostration—this is the gift of physical form.
"What is meant by the power of giving?

When a person cannot obtain food, their body becomes emaciated and their mind weak, such that they are unable to perform any tasks. Therefore, the wise provide them with food; thus, the act of giving food is the bestowing of power."

As for the power of giving, one possesses great strength in life after life; born among gods or humans, one's strength is peerless and without equal; whether moving in or out, advancing or halting, one's strength never diminishes—this is the power of giving.
"What is meant by 'bestowing peace and security'?

When a person lacks food, their mind is distressed and their body is precarious; they cannot remain settled in sitting or standing and find no self-composure. Therefore, the wise bestow food upon them; to bestow food is to bestow peace and security."

As for the gift of peace and security: one will be peaceful and secure in every lifetime; whether born among gods or humans, one will not encounter various calamities; wherever one goes, one will always meet with the worthy and virtuous; one’s wealth and resources will be immeasurable, and one will not suffer an untimely death or injury—this is called the gift of peace and security.
"What is meant by 'bestowing eloquence'?

When a person does not obtain food, their body becomes emaciated and their mind weakens, such that they are unable to speak. Therefore, the wise bestow food upon them; to bestow food is to bestow eloquence."

Those who bestowed eloquence were intelligent and wise in every lifetime; their speech was fluent and unhindered, and their wisdom and discernment were thoroughly penetrating. When born in the heavenly realms or the human world, those who heard them rejoiced, and there were none who did not bow their heads to listen to and receive their words of Dharma.
"These are the five blessings that are the retribution for the gift of food. The Buddha said:

"If sons or daughters of good family give rise to the aspiration for the Way and bestow all manner of food, drink, clothing, and bedding, they will, in whatever place they are born, behold the present Buddhas and receive instruction in the Three Dharmas. They shall attain the four applications of mindfulness, the three gates of liberation, and the ten powers; they shall possess the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics. Their movements throughout the ten directions will be like the rising sun, radiating brilliant light that shines everywhere upon the ten directions to transform and teach all beings. After their parinirvāṇa, the sutras and Dharma will continue to appear; by revering them, one attains deliverance no different from that of a Buddha."

When the Buddha had spoken these words, the devas, nāgas, spirits, and the people of the world—including sovereigns, great ministers, and the fourfold assembly of disciples—were all filled with joy and paid homage to the Buddha.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Five Kinds of Meritorious Retribution Obtained from Bestowing Food as Alms.
